== Course of events ==

After the commotion of being mistaken for Mary Ann by the White Rabbit and enduring the Pigeon's rants about her serpent-like neck, Alice finds herself speaking with the Caterpillar. Their discourse proves frustrating; the Caterpillar displays marked indifference to her attempts at conversation. Yet amidst this disagreeable exchange, the Caterpillar declares that he has something important to say. Upon hearing this promise, Alice agrees to remain and wait, willing to listen to whatever the Caterpillar means to impart.

This moment of agreement arrives despite the frustration that has characterized the conversation. The Caterpillar's indifference has made the exchange unsatisfying, yet his assurance of something of consequence to come proves enough to capture Alice's attention. She settles in to wait, prepared to hear what the Caterpillar promises to reveal.
